metadata.title: State-independent proof of Kochen-Specker theorem with 13 rays

nodes.name: Non-contextual hidden-variable model
nodes.statement: A model in which all observables have definite values determined by HVs $\lambda$ distributed according to $\varrho_\lambda$ with $\int d\lambda\varrho_\lambda=1$, where the value of an observable is independent of which compatible observable is measured alongside.
nodes.statement_clean: A hidden-variable model in which observable outcomes do not depend on the measurement context.

nodes.name: Context (maximal compatible set)
nodes.statement: A maximal set of mutually compatible observables, where two observables are compatible if they can be measured in a single experimental setup.

nodes.name: Product rule and sum rule
nodes.statement: Constraints imposed on HV models: the value assigned to the product (resp. sum) of two compatible observables equals the product (resp. sum) of the values assigned to those two observables.

nodes.name: KS value assignment
nodes.statement: An assignment of values $\{0,1\}$ to all rays of a Hilbert space such that: (1) the value of a ray is independent of which basis it lies in, and (2) one and only one ray is assigned value $1$ in any complete orthonormal basis.
nodes.statement_clean: A binary $\{0,1\}$-valued labeling of rays that is basis-independent and assigns exactly one $1$ per orthonormal basis.

nodes.name: Qutrit ray representation
nodes.statement: In basis $\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|2\rangle\}$ a qutrit ray $\hat r=|r\rangle\langle r|/\langle r|r\rangle$ is represented by the triple $r=(a,b,c)$ with $|r\rangle=a|0\rangle+b|1\rangle+c|2\rangle$.

nodes.name: Thirteen rays of the magic cube
nodes.statement: The set of 13 qutrit rays $\{y_k^\pm,h_\alpha,z_k\}$ with $y_k^\pm$ ($k=1,2,3$, $\sigma=\pm$), $h_\alpha$ ($\alpha=0,1,2,3$), and $z_k$ ($k=1,2,3$), determined by 26 points on the surface of a $3\times 3$ magic cube.
nodes.statement_clean: The 13 qutrit rays $\{y_k^\pm, h_\alpha, z_k\}$ used in the state-independent KS proof.

nodes.name: Orthogonality graph $\Delta_{13}$
nodes.statement: Graph with the 13 rays as vertices and edges between vertices iff the corresponding rays are orthogonal; its $13\times 13$ adjacency matrix $\Gamma$ has $\Gamma_{uv}=1$ for neighbors and $0$ otherwise (zero diagonal).

nodes.name: Dichotomic observables $\hat A_v$
nodes.statement: For each ray $\hat r_v\in\{\hat y_k^\sigma,\hat h_\alpha,\hat z_k\}$ define the dichotomic observable $\hat A_v=I-2\hat r_v$ with eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

nodes.name: Kochen-Specker theorem
nodes.statement: Non-contextual hidden-variable models cannot reproduce all the predictions of quantum mechanics; equivalently, in any Hilbert space of dimension $>2$ there exists a finite set of rays admitting no KS value assignment.
assumptions: HV model preserves the partial algebraic structure of compatible observables
conclusions: No KS value assignment exists for some finite ray set
Non-contextual HV models cannot reproduce QM predictions

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the 13-ray realization
nodes.statement: The 13 rays of Eq.~(\ref{r}) are determined uniquely (up to a global unitary) by the orthogonality relationships specified by the graph $\Delta_{13}$.
conclusions: Up to a global unitary, the 13 rays $\{y_k^\pm,h_\alpha,z_k\}$ are unique

nodes.name: At-most-one-$h_\alpha$ lemma
nodes.statement: In any KS value assignment to the 13 rays, at most one ray among $\{\hat h_\alpha\mid\alpha=0,1,2,3\}$ can be assigned the value $1$.
assumptions: Conditions 1 and 2 of a KS value assignment

nodes.name: State-independent KS proof for qutrit (original-rule version)
nodes.statement: Non-contextual HV models that preserve the algebraic structure of compatible observables must satisfy $\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\langle\hat h_\alpha\rangle_c\le 1$, but QM predicts $\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\langle\hat h_\alpha\rangle_q=4/3$ via the identity $\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\hat h_\alpha=\tfrac{4}{3}I$. Hence the KS theorem holds with only 13 rays.
assumptions: Non-contextual HV model with KS value assignment
Product and sum rules on compatible observables
conclusions: The inequality $\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\langle\hat h_\alpha\rangle_c\le 1$ is violated by QM ($=4/3$)

nodes.name: Combinatorial inequality on $\Delta_{13}$
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $a_v\in\{\pm 1\}$ ($v\in V$), $\sum_{v\in V} a_v - \tfrac14 \sum_{u,v\in V}\Gamma_{uv} a_u a_v \le 8$.

nodes.name: Magic-cube inequality (state-independent KS inequality)
nodes.statement: Every non-contextual HV model satisfies $\sum_{v\in V}\langle A_v\rangle_c-\tfrac14\sum_{u,v\in V}\Gamma_{uv}\langle A_u\cdot A_v\rangle_c\le 8$, while QM predicts this expectation equals $25/3>8$ for every qutrit state.
assumptions: Compatible-observable correlations as predicted by QM must be reproduced
conclusions: Quantum value: $\langle\hat L\rangle_q=25/3$ for all qutrit states
State-independent violation by all qutrit states

nodes.name: Operator identity $\hat L=\tfrac{25}{3}I$
nodes.statement: Defining $\hat L=\sum_{v\in V}\hat A_v-\tfrac14\sum_{u,v\in V}\Gamma_{uv}\hat A_u\hat A_v$, simple calculation using $\hat y=2I$, $\hat h=\tfrac{4}{3}I$, $\hat z=I$, and orthogonality-implied $\hat r_u\hat r_v=0$ when $\Gamma_{uv}=1$ yields $\hat L=\tfrac{25}{3}I$.
assumptions: $\Delta_{13}$ has 24 edges; $\hat r_u\hat r_v=0$ when $u,v$ adjacent

nodes.name: Original-rule KS inequality
nodes.statement: $\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\langle\hat h_\alpha\rangle_c:=\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\int d\lambda\,\varrho_\lambda h_\alpha^\lambda\le 1$.

nodes.name: Magic-cube inequality (operator form)
nodes.statement: $\sum_{v\in V}\langle A_v\rangle_c-\tfrac14\sum_{u,v\in V}\Gamma_{uv}\langle A_u\cdot A_v\rangle_c\le 8$.

nodes.name: Operator-sum identities
nodes.statement: $\hat y:=\sum_{k,\sigma}\hat y_k^\sigma=2I$, $\hat h:=\sum_{\alpha=0}^3\hat h_\alpha=\tfrac{4}{3}I$, $\hat z:=\sum_{k=1}^3\hat z_k=I$.

nodes.name: Proof of uniqueness of the 13-ray realization
nodes.statement: By choosing $z_k$ as the standard basis and using mutual orthogonality $\{z_k,y_k^\pm\}$ and $h_\alpha\perp y_{k-1}^+$, derive constraints $|t_k|=1$ and $t_1 t_2 t_3=1$, then apply a diagonal unitary fixing $h_0=(1,1,1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of at-most-one-$h_\alpha$
nodes.statement: By symmetry of $\Delta_{13}$ it suffices to consider two cases of two $\hat h_\alpha$ assigned $1$; both lead to a contradiction with condition 2 (one ray $=1$ per basis).

nodes.name: Proof of state-independent KS proof (original-rule)
nodes.statement: Integrating the bound $\sum_\alpha h_\alpha^\lambda\le 1$ against $\varrho_\lambda$ gives the classical inequality; QM gives $4/3$ via $\sum_\alpha\hat h_\alpha=\tfrac{4}{3}I$.

nodes.name: Proof of combinatorial inequality on $\Delta_{13}$
nodes.statement: Counting argument on $L=1+t+f-2l$, where $t,f,l$ count $-1$-valued vertices, $-1$-valued degree-4 vertices, and adjacent $-1$-pairs; case analysis on $t\in\{0,\dots,6\}$ shows $L\le 8$.

nodes.name: Proof of operator identity $\hat L=\tfrac{25}{3}I$
nodes.statement: Expand $\hat L=\sum_v(I-2\hat r_v)-\tfrac14\sum\Gamma_{uv}(I-2\hat r_u)(I-2\hat r_v)$, use $\sum_{uv}\Gamma_{uv}/2=24$ edges, vertex-degree counts (9 vertices of degree 4 and 4 of degree 3), and $\hat r_u\hat r_v=0$ when adjacent, to obtain $\hat L=I+2(\hat z+\hat y)+\hat h=\tfrac{25}{3}I$.

nodes.name: Case (i): $\hat h_0,\hat h_1$ both assigned 1
nodes.statement: If $\hat h_0$ and $\hat h_1$ are assigned value $1$, then $\hat y_2^\pm$ and $\hat y_3^\pm$ must be $0$, forcing both $\hat z_2$ and $\hat z_3$ to be assigned $1$ — impossible.

nodes.name: Case (ii): $\hat h_1,\hat h_2$ both assigned 1
nodes.statement: If $\hat h_1$ and $\hat h_2$ are assigned $1$, then $\hat y_1^\pm$ and $\hat y_2^\pm$ are $0$, forcing both $\hat z_1$ and $\hat z_2$ to be assigned $1$ — contradiction.

nodes.name: Setup: variables $t,f,l$ and identity $L=1+t+f-2l$
nodes.statement: Let $t$ be the total number of $a_v=-1$, $f$ the number of degree-4 vertices with $a_v=-1$, and $l$ the number of adjacent pairs both $-1$. Then $L=1+t+f-2l$ and by symmetry $a_v\mapsto -a_v$ we may assume $t\le 6$.

nodes.name: Case $t\le 3$
nodes.statement: Since $l\ge 0$ and $f\le t\le 3$, $L\le 1+3+3=7$.

nodes.name: Case $t=4$
nodes.statement: Among any 4 degree-4 vertices at least one connected pair exists, so it is impossible to have $f=4,l=0$. Hence $f-2l\le 3$ and $L\le 8$, attained at $f=3,l=0$ (e.g. $z_1,y_2^-,y_3^+,h_3$).

nodes.name: Case $t=5$
nodes.statement: If $f=5$ then $l\ge 2$, giving $L\le 7$. If $f\le 4$ then $l\ge 1$, giving $L\le 8$ (attained e.g. by $z_1,y_2^-,y_3^+,y_1^-,h_3$).

nodes.name: Case $t=6$
nodes.statement: If $f=6$, $l\ge 3$ so $L\le 7$; if $2\le f\le 5$ then $l\ge 2$ so $L\le 8$; if $f=1$ or $f=0$ then $L\le 7$.

nodes.name: Conclude: $L\le 8$ overall
nodes.statement: Combining all cases, $L=\sum_v a_v-\tfrac14\sum_{u,v}\Gamma_{uv}a_u a_v\le 8$.

nodes.name: Expand $\hat L$ in $\hat r_v$
nodes.statement: Substituting $\hat A_v=I-2\hat r_v$ gives $\hat L=13I-2(\hat y+\hat h+\hat z)-\tfrac{I}{4}\sum_{uv}\Gamma_{uv}+\sum_{uv}\Gamma_{uv}\hat r_v-\sum_{uv}\Gamma_{uv}\hat r_u\hat r_v$.

nodes.name: Apply edge count and orthogonality
nodes.statement: Using $\sum_{uv}\Gamma_{uv}=2\cdot 24=48$ and $\hat r_u\hat r_v=0$ when $\Gamma_{uv}=1$, plus degree counts (4 around $\hat z,\hat y$, 3 around $\hat h$): $\hat L=13I-2(\hat y+\hat h+\hat z)-12I+4(\hat z+\hat y)+3\hat h$.

nodes.name: Substitute identities $\hat y=2I,\hat h=\tfrac{4}{3}I,\hat z=I$
nodes.statement: Simplifies to $\hat L=I+2(\hat z+\hat y)+\hat h=I+2(I+2I)+\tfrac{4}{3}I=\tfrac{25}{3}I$.

nodes.name: Conditions of a KS value assignment
nodes.statement: (1) The value $\{0,1\}$ assigned to a ray is independent of the basis it lies in. (2) In any complete orthonormal basis exactly one ray is assigned value $1$.

nodes.name: State-independent KS test for qutrit
nodes.statement: Find an experimentally testable inequality involving as few qutrit observables as possible that is satisfied by all non-contextual HV models but violated by all qutrit states, providing a state-independent test of quantum contextuality.

nodes.name: 13 is the minimal ray count (conjecture)
nodes.statement: We conjecture that the KS theorem does not have a state-independent proof using fewer than 13 rays.
conclusions: No state-independent KS proof exists with fewer than 13 rays

nodes.name: Comparison with prior KS proofs
nodes.statement: The original Kochen-Specker proof uses 117 rays, Peres' and Schuttle's use 33, the Conway-Kochen proof uses 31 rays, and the best 4-state-system proof (Cabello et al.) uses 18; this paper achieves 13 for the qutrit.

nodes.name: Lifting product/sum rules via two-observable correlations
nodes.statement: The product and sum rules can be dropped if one only requires HV models to reproduce QM predictions on sequential measurements (correlations of compatible observables); this imposes no additional constraint beyond reproducing QM.

nodes.name: 3-box paradox in the proof
nodes.statement: Each 8-ray sub-set arising in cases (i)/(ii) (e.g. $\hat h_{0,1}$, $z_{2,3}$, $y_{2,3}^\pm$) constitutes a 3-box paradox, also appearing in Clifton's state-dependent KS proof and in compatibility-loophole proposals.

nodes.name: Experimental feasibility
nodes.statement: Only 13 observables and correlations of pairs of compatible observables are involved, so the test is within current technology — nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond are a promising platform.

nodes.name: Pentagram inequality (Klyachko et al.)
nodes.statement: A KS-type inequality based on a pentagon graph testing non-contextuality with only 5 dichotomic observables and two-observable correlations; state-dependent.
